extraction.Name: Louis Pourier
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to SC acre allotment when it was issued, for he figured that he would better off without it, leaving it under Government management; that he wrote to the Superintendent of the Pine Ridge Agency to that effect; that he got notice that gradually the County would get it any how for taxes, so he accepted it
extraction.Buyer: R.C. Dessert, from Merriman, Nebraska; deponent signed a warranty deed in favor of Dessert written on a piece of paper torn from a common tablet by lawyer James Ryan; deed was not notarized; Dessert refused to give deed back but gave $400.00 through lawyer Charles Milner of Martin, South Dakota in the shape of a check
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: his taxes got behind, and, in 1920, he was having trouble with his first wife, she suing for divorce; that R.C. Dessert came to deponent and said this piece of land would be involved in the law-suit case, and if he gave a blind deed to it, when the trouble was over, Dessert would give it back and save the land
extraction.Occupation/Income: farms the children's allotments for a living
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has good health; married again, wife's health is not very good, she having liver trouble; has six children to support, but they have good health; it keeps him pretty busy to make ends meet; has never received any help from the County, State or United States Government; considers he was defrauded out of the land pure and simple; lawyer James Ryan's address is Martin, South Dakota; lawyer Charles Milner of Martin, South Dakota was also involved; deed was written on a piece of paper torn from a common tablet and was not notarized; deponent cashed the $400.00 check on advice of lawyer Milner who said 'Cash it; we will get this land back from him' but land was never recovered; sworn before Notary Public, Shannon County, South Dakota, November 26, 1928 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Pine Ridge Agency" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')

recovery_notes.rationale: Pine Ridge tribe field had 40+ string variants across the corpus. Consolidating to canonical 'Pine Ridge' for clean tabulation while preserving original variant in NOTES for audit.
